name: Paradesi Synagogue, Mattancherry
tagline: Kochi’s 16th‑century synagogue anchoring Jew Town’s heritage lane
summary: The Paradesi Synagogue (1568) in Mattancherry is Kochi’s historic Jewish house of worship and a highlight of the year‑round Mattancherry heritage circuit, from spice lanes to antique shops.
description: The Paradesi Synagogue is a 16th‑century Jewish house of worship at the end of Synagogue Lane in Mattancherry’s Jew Town. It houses Chinese hand‑painted tiles, Belgian glass chandeliers, Torah scrolls and royal gifts that tell the story of Cochin’s Jewish traders.

The synagogue matters as a living symbol of Kochi’s multicultural past and as one of the few functioning synagogues in Kerala. It anchors a compact heritage circuit — Mattancherry Palace, spice warehouses, antique lanes and the new Jewish museum — that culture travellers visit year‑round.

Visitors get a close, tactile heritage experience: a shaded walk through spice and antique shops, a guided look at the synagogue interior and artifacts, and now a nearby Jewish Museum that documents the community’s history and material culture.
highlights: 1568 synagogue with Chinese porcelain floor tiles and 19th‑century Belgian chandeliers
Carved teak ark holding Torah scrolls and historic copper plates
Synagogue Lane (Jew Town) with spice warehouses and antique shops
New Jewish Museum (opened 2026) next to the synagogue
Part of the compact Mattancherry heritage circuit — easy half‑day or full‑day loop

sections.heading: Background
body: The Paradesi Synagogue (also called the Mattancherry or Pardesi Syna gogue) dates to 1568 and sits on land granted to the Jewish community by the Raja of Cochin. It served Sephardic and other Jewish traders who settled in Kochi and has been repaired and restored over centuries.

The complex displays rare objects — copper plates recording early privileges, two royal gold crowns, a teak ark, and individually hand‑painted Chinese tiles — and remains a focal point for preserving Cochin Jewish heritage.

sections.heading: What to see and do
body: Step inside (shoes off) and view the blue‑and‑white Chinese porcelain floor tiles, the gilded women’s gallery, the brass‑railed pulpit and the chandeliers. Look for the carved teak ark where the scrolls of the Law are kept and the commemorative stones from other Kerala synagogues.
Walk Synagogue Lane and the spice‑warehouse streets nearby for antiques, textiles and Kerala curios. Add Mattancherry (Dutch) Palace and the Jewish Museum next door to round out the heritage circuit.

sections.heading: Plan your visit
body: Visiting hours listed by Kerala Tourism are Sunday–Thursday 10:00–18:00 and Friday 10:00–14:00; Saturday is listed as a holiday. Visitors enter barefoot and should dress modestly. Confirm hours and any closures (Jewish holidays, special services) before you go.

A Jewish Museum beside the synagogue opened in early 2026 and displays many newly catalogued artefacts; Onmanorama and local press report visiting hours and an entry fee for the museum (entry fees published at opening: ₹100 foreign tourists, ₹50 others) — confirm current fees on arrival.

Mattancherry sits within easy reach of Ernakulam: take the public ferry or Kochi Water Metro to Mattancherry/Mattancherry Jetty and walk the spice lanes to Synagogue Lane, or use an auto/taxi from Fort Kochi or Ernakulam. The Mattancherry Water Metro terminal opened October 11, 2025, making water access easier for heritage walkers.

latest.text: Feature coverage highlights the dwindling local Jewish community and the importance of the synagogue and new museum for preserving Cochin Jewish memory.
A Jewish Museum beside the Paradesi Synagogue opens in Mattancherry to document Cochin’s Jewish history; visiting hours and entry fees are published at opening.
Local reports note the Paradesi Synagogue museum underwent a security overhaul and was set to reopen after earlier soft launches and police review.

visitorInfo.bestTime: Year‑round; best for sightseeing in the dry, cooler months (October–February).
visitorInfo.howToReach: From Ernakulam take the passenger ferry or Kochi Water Metro to Mattancherry/Mattancherry Jetty, then walk about 5–10 minutes along the spice and antique lanes to Synagogue Lane; taxis or autos from Fort Kochi/Ernakulam are also quick.
etiquette: Shoes are removed before entering the synagogue — wear easy‑to‑remove footwear and modest clothing.
Synagogue and museum schedules change for Jewish holidays, services and security reviews — confirm opening times on the day you visit.
Combine the synagogue with Mattancherry Palace, Jew Town lanes and spice warehouses for a half‑day heritage loop.
Respect photography rules inside the synagogue and follow guidance from trustees or guides.
